title: Dispatch BBA 6: Sister Kells Opens the East Ward
summary: The missing nurse says the hospital has been calling its dead back to discharge them.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Sister Beatrice Kells met Dr. Saye and Miss Morrow at the east ward door yesterday. She appeared as she had in photographs from 1874, wearing the white apron and cap of her order. Her hands were steady. She did not seem aware that the hospital above her had burned.

Sister Kells said she carried the discharge ledger out of the burning ward but could not leave its pages behind. "I was meant to record every departure," she said. "One child left before I could write her name. The ward has kept the door open ever since."

The ledger contains forty-one entries recording death or release on the night of the fire. It has no record of Elsie Gray. Sister Kells said she remembered the child's face but not her name. "I called her the forty-second patient," she said. "I have been waiting to close the book."

Miss Morrow showed her evidence that Elsie Gray survived. Sister Kells remembered the child. "The ledger will accept any hand that writes the truth," she said. "Enter her name and the date she left. The ward will finish its record and let the rest go."

Dr. Saye says the remaining task is precise: identify Patient 42 in the admission register, enter her discharge date in the ledger, and allow the ward to complete the record it has maintained since 1874.
